name: Urdu alphabet (Nastaliq)
signature: Right-to-left words descend diagonally in calligraphic Nastaliq, with dense joins and carefully placed dots.
combination: Letters join right-to-left and change shape by position. Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq; the bundled Naskh font is currently a readable fallback while the course data records Nastaliq structure. Short vowels are normally omitted.
notes: Starter inventory for the first Urdu shared-spine lessons, grounded in Zer o Zabar. This canonical script-data file keeps Noto Naskh as its readable path-checking fallback; the book and Language Ladder presentation use the separately vendored Noto Nastaliq Urdu family. The full letter inventory remains explicit next-track work.

strokeOrderSource.variation: The lesson explicitly distinguishes independent ا, drawn top-to-bottom in one continuous stroke, from final ـا, drawn bottom-to-top. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback.

strokeOrderSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, Te, mim, jim, che, and more diacritics, independent ج handwriting animation and flat-head insight (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form animation places the dot below first, lifts once, then draws the pointed hooked head, descent, and bowl in one continuous stroke. The lesson says the back corner should be pointed rather than rounded and documents a flat-head alternative as purely aesthetic. This learner path covers the pointed independent form and fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback.

strokeOrder: continue curving to the left without lifting

strokeOrderSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, Dāl, re, and wāw, independent ر handwriting animation and Re instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form animation and adjacent prose show one uninterrupted stroke: draw a downward line, then curve to the left. The final form instead drops sharply to the lower left from the preceding letter. The lesson also notes that final re rises in Naskh but not in Nastaliq. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback.
